Background

A bit about my background and how I work.

Where I studied, what I've worked on over the past few years, and what I enjoy outside of software.

I'm a software engineer based in Ruwa, Zimbabwe. I've always liked figuring out how systems work under the hood. That curiosity led me to study Computer Science at the National University of Science and Technology (NUST) in Bulawayo, where I graduated with an Honours degree (2.1) in 2024.

Working in Production ERP

For the past two years, I've worked at M&J SERPA, an official Odoo partner. Working on ERP systems teaches you quickly that software isn't theoretical. It touches real payroll runs, inventory movements, and customer billing.

Across more than 50 production client setups, I've focused heavily on tax compliance integrations. In Zimbabwe, I built integrations for the ZIMRA Fiscal Device Management System (FDMS). In Zambia, I set up connections for ZRA SmartInvoice. When a fiscal integration fails, physical checkout lines stop and companies face tax penalties. That pressure taught me to write careful, thoroughly tested Python code, optimize database queries, and plan for network drops from day one.

“Simplicity is prerequisite for reliability.” — Edsger W. Dijkstra

Outside of Work

I'm an introvert, so I recharge in quiet spaces. When I step away from my laptop, I usually spend my time on a few things that keep my mind active:

I play a lot of chess under the handle knightking_zw on Chess.com. My favorite way to play is Chess960 (Fischer Random), where the pieces on the back rank are shuffled at the start of each match. It cuts out memorized openings entirely and forces you to evaluate positions from scratch. I also solve sudoku puzzles daily — simple logic, clear rules, and no shortcuts.

Reading and writing are part of my daily routine. I keep a journal to review decisions, note mistakes, and plan my work before opening a code editor. On my bookshelf, you'll find Marcus Aurelius and Alan Watts alongside books on discipline like Hagakure, plus science fiction like Andy Weir's Project Hail Mary.

When I need to focus on a difficult bug, I put on headphones. My music rotates between hip-hop lyricists (J. Cole, Kendrick Lamar), rock (Linkin Park), Hans Zimmer film scores, and instrumental lofi tracks.
